current_activity: Belfort Gap offensive: under the I Corps the division moves along the Swiss border and captures Delle
notes: Event date: 18 November 1944 (Wikipedia; CMH Riviera to the Rhine, p. 420). Event definition: Attacking from the upper Doubs valley on 14 November under the I Corps, the division manoeuvres along the French-Swiss border toward Hericourt and captures Delle on 18 November, its supply route for the drive to the Rhine. Event support: two source families (Wikipedia and the US Army official history (CMH)). Wikipedia, 1st Armored Division (France), section Combat for Alsace November 14, 1944 to February 9, 1945: "Operating under the 1st Army Corps of General Antoine Béthouart, it manoeuvred to Héricourt along the French-Swiss border and captured Delle on November 18"; CMH Riviera to the Rhine ch. 23 p. 420: "The 1st Armored Division's CC3 had poked out a very slender salient to the Rhine, and its supply routes east from Delle were extremely vulnerable". Location: Delle, Territoire de Belfort (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location support: Wikipedia names Delle and the date; the CMH history names Delle as the start of the supply routes of the division on 19 November; two source families. Commander: Maj. Gen. Jean Touzet du Vigier commands the division (Wikipedia: 1 May 1943 to 8 January 1945).

commander: Maj. Gen. Jean Touzet du Vigier
source_locator: R651: p. 419; R680: section Combat for Alsace November 14, 1944 to February 9, 1945
current_activity: First Allied unit to reach the Rhine: an advance detachment of combat command 3 reaches the river at Rosenau
notes: Event date: 19 November 1944 (CMH Riviera to the Rhine, p. 419; Wikipedia). Event definition: Combat command 3 drives east from Courtelevant; in the afternoon an advance detachment avoids the German defenses on back roads and reaches the Rhine at Rosenau a little after 1800. Event support: two source families (the US Army official history (CMH) and Wikipedia). CMH Riviera to the Rhine ch. 23 p. 419: "To the south CC3, starting out from Courtelevant before dawn, headed eastward in three columns"; "During the afternoon of the 19th, an advance detachment of the command swung off along back roads; it avoided almost all German defenses and reached the Rhine at Rosenau"; Wikipedia, 1st Armored Division (France), section Combat for Alsace November 14, 1944 to February 9, 1945: "the CC3 was in Alsace and, at 1800, the tank platoon of Lieutenant Loisy was able to raise its standard on the banks of the Rhine at Rosenau". Location: Rosenau, Haut-Rhin (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location approximate: the point is the place of the advance detachment; the rest of the division is to the west. Location support: both sources name Rosenau; the point is the place of an advance detachment of one combat command. Commander: Maj. Gen. Jean Touzet du Vigier commands the division (Wikipedia: 1 May 1943 to 8 January 1945).

current_activity: Enters Mulhouse; on 23 November units of the division fight the 106th Panzer Brigade there
notes: Event date: 20 November 1944 (Wikipedia); 23 November (CMH Riviera to the Rhine, p. 427). Event definition: From the Rhine the division turns north: Colonel Caldairou enters Mulhouse on 20 November, and on 23-24 November units of the division repulse the 106th Panzer Brigade east and southeast of the city. Event support: two source families (Wikipedia and the US Army official history (CMH)). Wikipedia, 1st Armored Division (France), section Combat for Alsace November 14, 1944 to February 9, 1945: "during the attack on the Lefebvre barracks at Mulhouse. On 20 November, Colonel Caldairou entered the city"; CMH Riviera to the Rhine ch. 23 p. 427: "During the afternoon of 23 November, as the 106th Panzer Brigade moved toward Mulhouse reinforced by several weak infantry battalions, it ran up against units of the 1st Armored Division". Location: Mulhouse, Haut-Rhin with a precision of 3 km. Location support: Wikipedia names Mulhouse for 20 November; the CMH history places units of the division at Mulhouse on 23 November; two source families. Commander: Maj. Gen. Jean Touzet du Vigier commands the division (Wikipedia: 1 May 1943 to 8 January 1945).
